Subject: Commitment variance scaler questionnaire and burst plan intake

Hi Ami —

Great to meet earlier this week. To give you a crisp sizing recommendation for Dedicated (reserved + burst) and to model cost/latency tradeoffs, could you fill the attached CSV and answer the short questions below? If you can paste short sample traces (anonymized) that’s even better — a tokenized minute of representative traffic helps our runtime profiler.

What we need (short answers OK):
- Sustained baseline RPS (requests/sec) and average concurrency per session.
- Typical peak burst RPS and burst duration distribution (e.g., 2–5 min spikes, ~4x baseline).
- Average prompt length (tokens) and average response length (tokens); percent of requests using streaming.
- Percent of inference requests that are session-affine (user-specific KV cache reuse).
- Observed KV cache hit rate for session-affine requests (if tracked).
- Acceptable quality delta for fallback/quantized variants (e.g., <5% fidelity drop), and whether int8/int4 quantization is desired.
- Preferred GPU SKUs or any hardware constraints.
- Target p50/p95/p99 token latency objectives (e.g., p99 <= 300ms).
- Monthly committed GPU hours or concurrency target you’re thinking about (if any).
- Important dayparts (local peak windows) and regional distribution (if multi-region).
- Any nightly batch/async processing windows we can leverage for non-real-time work.

Attachments: commitment-variance-template.csv (simple CSV to copy/paste sample rows), sample tokenized trace format in the Drive link.

Goal: produce an initial sizing matrix (sustained commit, prewarm pool, autoscale ceiling) and a recommended burst strategy (prewarm / instant scale / model fallbacks) so your procurement and legal teams can evaluate cost vs. SLA.

If it helps, I can run a quick estimate from whatever sample trace you have and follow up with a short 30–45m sizing walkthrough.

Thanks —
Markus Klein

Thanks Markus — attaching a small sample trace and a partially-completed CSV. See answers inline below; I’ll follow up if our procurement/legal folks have contract questions.

- Sustained baseline RPS: 12 RPS (steady-state). Average concurrency per active session: ~1.3.
- Peak bursts: typical campaign-driven bursts ~260 RPS; we observe extreme bursts up to ~1,200 RPS for 1–3 minutes (rare, ~1% of days).
- Avg prompt length: 55 tokens; avg response length: 220 tokens. ~30% of calls use streaming.
- Session-affinity: ~60% of requests reuse a per-user session; KV cache hit-rate on those requests: ~45%.
- Quantization: we’re open to int8. Int4 acceptable for non-critical paths if model quality checks out.
- Quality tolerance for fallback: up to ~20% quality regression is tolerated for short windows if a fast fallback keeps throughput.
- Target latency (token): p50 40ms, p95 120ms, p99 target <= 250ms.
- Regional distribution: 75% US west, 20% US east, 5% EU.
- Proposed commit: we don’t have buy-side experience for GPUs — open to your recommendation. Billing cadence: monthly preferred.
- Nightly batch windows: we have a 01:00–03:00 UTC window for offline re-ranking/batch jobs.

Attached: lumina-traffic-sample.jsonl (10k anonymized requests, tokenized).

Ami Gupta

Markus — quick clarifying note for the intake CSV before we run the estimator:
- Can we map the customer-provided RPS to concurrency for their largest model variant (i.e., currentsize tokens/sec => ops/sec)? We should ask whether their 1,200 RPS extreme bursts are single-shard or multi-origin (many users spiking simultaneously) — that changes prewarm sizing.
- Also confirm their batching window: are they currently aggregating requests (server-side) with a 50–100ms batching window, or sending per-request?

If Ami can confirm those two points we’ll include a prewarm-warm-pool suggestion and an autoscale ceiling, plus an expected monthly committed GPU hours estimate. I’ll block time for a 45m sizing call; Markus, can you take the lead on the capacity sketch?

— Marissa

Ami — thanks for the quick turnaround and the tokenized trace. Preliminary read (high-level):

- Recommended starting commit: 12 A100-class GPUs (sustained) to cover baseline + steady growth with autoscale.
- Prewarm pool: maintain a 5–10 GPU warm pool (preloaded models + KV cache) to reduce cold-start p99 for short bursts.
- Autoscale ceiling: configure autoscale to 60 GPUs to cover 1,200 RPS short spikes; combine with fast fallback routing to an int8 variant for non-critical traffic.
- KV cache: set per-session KV retention to 12 hours for your workload; projected cache hit-rate gains reduce steady token cost by ~8–10% in our model.
- Quantization: recommend int8 for primary production path; reserve int4 for background/async re-ranking.
- Burst strategy: two-tier — instant scale to hot pool (minutes) + fallback to quantized model for first-line traffic, then gradual autoscale fill for heavier sustained bursts.
- Cost note: preliminary model suggests monthly committed GPU hours equivalent to ~12 GPUs with autoscale metered usage for bursts; we’ll convert to $/month once you confirm preferred GPU SKU and commitment term.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether bursts are single-shard (few clients generating many parallel requests) vs. fan-in (many clients each sending small numbers)?
2) Confirm batching window (50–100ms or per-request).
3) Quick sizing call: I propose Wed 2029-06-26 10:00 PDT / 13:00 EDT for a 45m session. I’ll seed a calendar invite once you confirm.

Attaching an updated CSV template with our initial placement suggestions. Also linking a short runbook we’ll use during the call.

Thanks —
